summary: Catalan has ser/ésser and estar, but their distribution is not Spanish: simple location often uses ser, while estar is important for states, duration/residence, and many resultative patterns; haver-hi is existential.

semantic_map.SEM.CHARACTERISTIC_PROPERTY: ser/ésser for many defining/inherent properties; adjective-specific patterns require review
semantic_map.SEM.CURRENT_STATE: estar for many temporary/situational states; some predicates prefer ser
semantic_map.SEM.RESULTANT_STATE: estar or ser + participle/adjective depending result vs inherent/passive reading
semantic_map.SEM.ENTITY_LOCATION: ser for simple location in standard Catalan; estar/estar-se for duration/residence or licensed contexts
semantic_map.SEM.EVENT_LOCATION: ser / tenir lloc according to event construction
semantic_map.SEM.ORIGIN_AFFILIATION: ser de / nationality or affiliation predicate
semantic_map.SEM.POSSESSION_AS_EXISTENCE: ordinary possession uses tenir; haver-hi is existential, not a general possessive replacement
